narrative.what_i_did:
Session resumed with PLAN.md Tier 1 items 2 through 5 complete and item 6 (multi-device sync honest UX) as the last carpenter-side Tier 1 item. I opened with a chip-form chooser offering item 6 as either the local-newer-than-cloud indicator on the home screen banner or the WalletGuide-doc variant, plus pause-for-field-test. The operator picked the indicator path.

I grounded against the sync substrate by reading walletStore.ts (last-write-wins coordinator that always writes local and conditionally writes remote, returning a SaveOutcome with localSyncedAt + remoteSyncedAt + remoteFailed), prefsStore.ts (the Prefs type carrying cloudSync + lastRemoteSync + theme + idle timeout etc, with prefsStore.load merging saved prefs over a defaults object — migration-safe for any new field), and HomeScreen.tsx's inlined backupBanner function which already had three honest cases (cloud-sync off → wallet lives only on this device, lastRemoteSync null → first sync pending, lastRemoteSync age greater than 24h → stale). The gap was clear: when remote push fails or is deferred while the local save lands, the operator sees no signal that the cloud is behind their device until 24 hours have elapsed.

The cleanest cut was to add a new `lastLocalSync` ISO timestamp field to Prefs that always advances when walletStore.save completes locally, regardless of remote outcome. The banner uses lastLocalSync > lastRemoteSync as the honest signal for 'local changes have not reached the cloud yet' and surfaces an amber message with copy 'Local changes have not reached the cloud yet — they are safe on this device but not yet backed up. The next save will try again.' The new branch was placed in priority order BEFORE the stale-cloud check so when both are true (cloud is more than a day old AND local is newer than that), the more specific and more actionable message wins. Migration-safe by default — prefsStore.load merges saved prefs over the defaults object so pre-existing wallets inherit lastLocalSync=null and the new banner branch stays inactive until the next save advances it.

I also extracted backupBanner from inline-inside-HomeScreen into a sibling backupBanner.ts module. The function had grown to five branches with priority ordering that mattered, and the helper was prime test material — extracting let me lock the behavior with 8 tests covering each branch plus the priority-order invariant (local-newer wins over stale-cloud when both true) plus the null-lastLocalSync migration safety case. STALE_AFTER_MS moved with the function and is re-exported. HomeScreen now imports backupBanner from the sibling module, no behavior change.

The walletStore.save edits ran in three branches matching the three paths: cloudSync off → write local, set lastLocalSync, return; cloudSync on remote-succeeded → write local, write remote, set both lastLocalSync and lastRemoteSync atomically, return; cloudSync on remote-failed → write local, set lastLocalSync only, return with remoteFailed=true. The atomic two-field update in the success path is important so a successful save lands with lastLocalSync === lastRemoteSync and the banner does not flicker between 'all good' and 'local newer' between the two prefs writes. WalletProvider's initial prefs state gained lastLocalSync: null for completeness.

Manifest updates: storage manifest gained a leading paragraph in notes describing the lastLocalSync field, its always-advances semantics, the home-screen banner's use of it, and the migration-safety property. Wallet-core manifest gained backupBanner.ts and backupBanner.test.ts in touches.

All four gates green throughout — typecheck silent, lint silent, 350 of 350 tests passing in 10.51s (gained 8 from the new backupBanner tests), build clean with HomeScreen at 22.27KB gz under the 22.5KB budget, WalletProvider unchanged at 9.58KB gz, login bundle unchanged at 11.30KB gz. One commit this session — 0b891ec for the local-newer-than-cloud banner surface and the backupBanner extraction.

narrative.what_you_could_do_better:
Two observations. First, the lastLocalSync field is now part of the persisted Prefs payload, but the existing Prefs migration via prefsStore.load defaults merging only covers the FIRST load after the field was added — subsequent saves persist whatever was on the object at save time. This works because every save path I touched now sets lastLocalSync explicitly, but if a future code path saves prefs WITHOUT going through walletStore.save (e.g. a direct prefsStore.save call from settings), it could inadvertently drop the field by spreading a stale prefs object. The pattern that would prevent this is having prefsStore.save merge the saved value into the defaults at write time too, but that risks overwriting fields the caller explicitly set to null. Honest tradeoff — the current shape is correct under the conventions the codebase already uses, and a future migration concern can be addressed when it arises.

Second, I did not add a 'sync now' button in the banner itself. The PLAN.md item 6 description said 'honest UX' and named the surfacing as the load-bearing fix. The current banner is informational and tells the operator the next save will retry, which is true because most operator gestures (new entry, new handshake, new presence) trigger an implicit save. But a button labeled 'Try syncing now' that calls the useWallet().save() callback would close the loop more actively — operator sees the banner, taps the button, banner clears. That is a small additional cut that would feel more closed but is structurally separate from the surfacing work I did here. If the field-test surfaces frustration with the implicit-retry pattern, the button is a one-line addition.

Nothing else surfaced beyond the declared scope this session.
narrative.bigger_picture:
The bigger-picture teaching this session is the closure of a multi-session arc. PLAN.md was written 2026-05-28 morning to consolidate the audit's findings into a tiered priority order for Bitcoin-community evaluation readiness. Across five sessions (this one and four prior) all five carpenter-side Tier 1 items have shipped cleanly — RecoveryInitiatorModal extracted, FreshOnboarding extracted, OTS calendar end-state surfaced, Bitcoin tab framing added, local-newer-than-cloud banner added. Each cut was small, each landed under the four-gates discipline, each preserved bundle budgets or honestly bumped them with documenting comments. The carpenter side of the embarrassment-gap-closing arc is done; only the operator's hardware field-test of the recovery substrate remains before Tier 3 (the Matt Odell tribute attestation) becomes the next active thread. This is exactly the leverage the audit-plus-roadmap pattern was meant to create — the prioritization was done once, the work was executed mechanically against it, the substrate moved from 75% community-evaluation-ready toward as-ready-as-carpenter-side-can-make-it.

The second teaching is the value of consistently extracting growing inline functions into testable helpers. backupBanner started as an 11-line inline function in HomeScreen with three branches and grew to a 30-line function with five branches and priority-order semantics. Extracting it into a sibling module with 8 tests took roughly two minutes and locked the priority order behavior so a future addition (a sixth case, a re-ordering, a copy edit) cannot silently regress the semantics. This is the same pattern the prior session's deriveVerificationStatus extraction followed — when a function's branches multiply or its logic acquires invariants, the extract-and-test cut is cheap and the regression-protection is durable. The wallet's substrate gets structurally tighter while the visible product gets slightly better, which is the right ratio at this stage.

The broader thesis-level connection is what 'community-evaluation-ready' means in practice. A Bitcoin community evaluator opening this wallet today sees a substrate that has been thinking honestly about its own gaps — the doctrine answers are in-wallet (Bitcoin tab), the silent debts have been surfaced (OTS calendar-slow, local-newer-than-cloud), the structural prep for the next forced extractions has been done (RecoveryInitiatorModal, FreshOnboarding), and the test discipline holds across 350 tests. This is the substrate-readiness arc closing. The cross-device recovery test the operator runs next is the test of the test discipline — if recovery actually works end-to-end across two devices, the wallet's core sovereign-identity claim is provable in front of evaluators. If it surfaces issues, those issues have headroom to land their fixes in the right places. Either way the substrate has been prepared honestly for the moment. Two cuts down today, six cuts down across the branch, one operator field-test left.

feedback_to_appcommander: Tier 1 carpenter-side closure across five sessions is a clean execution of the audit-plus-roadmap pattern. The PLAN.md document written 2026-05-28 morning consolidated 23 manifest pending notes plus the doctrine quintet plus the file-size warnings plus the operator's strategy threads into a single tiered priority order; from there each session opened with a chip-form chooser sourced from the roadmap and the cut executed mechanically.
